acceptance_signals: AGENTS.md requires every completed feature handoff to state what was completed, the short-term benefits, the long-term benefits, the next proposed feature, and how the two features connect.
The instructions keep the next feature human-controlled and require explicit unknown or not-yet-decided wording when repository evidence does not establish it.
A deterministic documentation test protects the required completion-handoff phrases.
STATUS.md and the current development log record the workflow change without changing runtime, product contract, release identity, or consumer behavior.
Relevant tests, task and repository checks, scope review, and git diff validation pass before any explicitly authorized commit and ordinary non-force push to origin main.

decision.rationale: On 2026-08-14 the completion handoff contract was extended from four to seven required questions covering the completed capability, short-term benefits, long-term benefits, upstream capability, proposed next feature, feature-to-feature connection, and whole-project benefit. Evidence-bounded and human-owned roadmap language is protected by documentation tests. Eight focused tests, 42 combined documentation/task tests, and the complete 806-test suite passed with 2 skips; repository governance had no failure. A bounded current-Agent review found no requirement, scope, or authority drift. This paused task authorizes no follow-on implementation; the separately explicit human Git authorization is handled only through the repository Git procedure.

requirement.summary: Update the repository Agent instructions so every completed feature handoff states what was completed, its short-term benefits, its long-term benefits, the next proposed feature, and how the completed and next features connect.

items: Ambiguous wording could let an Agent invent long-term benefits or an unauthorized roadmap commitment.
The new template could duplicate or contradict the existing four-question completion communication contract.
A mixed working tree could cause unrelated human-owned files to be staged unless Git scope is inspected and explicit.
Reviewed assumption: The new benefit-linked handoff extends rather than replaces the existing completion communication requirements.
Reviewed assumption: Short-term and long-term benefits must remain evidence-bounded and may be unknown when not established.
Reviewed assumption: The user's explicit Git authorization applies only to the reviewed intended changes and an ordinary non-force push to origin main.
Reviewed unknown: The next product feature after Harness Contract v1 has not yet been selected.
Reviewed unknown: Existing untracked .codex content, the LinkedIn cover image, and the unrelated runtime-completion task remain outside this change and must not be staged.

title: Require benefit-linked completion handoffs
